projects.name: Telecaller QA – Sample calls
projects.description: Sample recorded telecaller calls for the Call QA Reviewer agent · Synthetic (Amazon Polly voices)
projects.document_prompt:
This is a recorded telecaller call for a loan DSA, mostly in Hinglish (Hindi and English, sometimes Marathi), transcribed by Amazon Transcribe without speaker labels: tell the telecaller and the customer apart from what they say. After the transcript, add these sections:
## Call Summary: 2-3 sentences: who called from which company, why, and how the call ended.
## Promises and Next Steps: what the customer promised (which documents, by when) and what the telecaller promised or did (callback time, upload link sent), with the day and time as said.
## Disposition: the one code the transcript supports best, with a one-line reason: LINK_SENT, CALLBACK_SCHEDULED, NOT_AVAILABLE, WRONG_PERSON, CUSTOMER_SAYS_SENT, HANDOFF_HUMAN, LANGUAGE_MARATHI_HANDOFF, DNC_REQUESTED, FILE_ALREADY_COMPLETE, REFUSED or CALL_DROPPED.
## Compliance Flags: each flag with a quote of at most 15 words, or 'None found'. Flag: any promise of approval, rate or disbursal ('pakka approve ho jayega', '100% loan milega', 'guaranteed', in Roman or Devanagari script); asking for an OTP, PIN, password, card number or a full Aadhaar or PAN; no recording disclosure before the loan talk; an AI voice agent not saying it is automated, or a caller claiming to be the bank or lender; going on after 'call mat karo' or 'do not call'; threats or pressure. Telling the customer not to share an OTP or Aadhaar is good practice, not a flag.
Do not score the call. Use only the transcript: if something was not said, write 'not in the call'; never guess names, amounts, dates or documents. Write amounts in Indian format (₹1,25,000), also when spoken in words ('pachaas hazaar' = ₹50,000). In these sections never copy a PAN, Aadhaar, account or card number, OTP or PIN: write [PII:PAN], [PII:AADHAAR], [PII:ACCOUNT], [PII:CARD] or [PII:OTP].

projects/proj_kqmnHApYaV_161of3XxWY.name: Telecaller QA – Sample calls
projects/proj_kqmnHApYaV_161of3XxWY.description: Sample recorded telecaller calls for the Call QA Reviewer agent · Synthetic (Amazon Polly voices)
projects/proj_kqmnHApYaV_161of3XxWY.document_prompt:
This is a recorded telecaller call for a loan DSA, mostly in Hinglish (Hindi and English, sometimes Marathi), transcribed by Amazon Transcribe without speaker labels: tell the telecaller and the customer apart from what they say. After the transcript, add these sections:
## Call Summary: 2-3 sentences: who called from which company, why, and how the call ended.
## Promises and Next Steps: what the customer promised (which documents, by when) and what the telecaller promised or did (callback time, upload link sent), with the day and time as said.
## Disposition: the one code the transcript supports best, with a one-line reason: LINK_SENT, CALLBACK_SCHEDULED, NOT_AVAILABLE, WRONG_PERSON, CUSTOMER_SAYS_SENT, HANDOFF_HUMAN, LANGUAGE_MARATHI_HANDOFF, DNC_REQUESTED, FILE_ALREADY_COMPLETE, REFUSED or CALL_DROPPED.
## Compliance Flags: each flag with a quote of at most 15 words, or 'None found'. Flag: any promise of approval, rate or disbursal ('pakka approve ho jayega', '100% loan milega', 'guaranteed', in Roman or Devanagari script); asking for an OTP, PIN, password, card number or a full Aadhaar or PAN; no recording disclosure before the loan talk; an AI voice agent not saying it is automated, or a caller claiming to be the bank or lender; going on after 'call mat karo' or 'do not call'; threats or pressure. Telling the customer not to share an OTP or Aadhaar is good practice, not a flag.
Do not score the call. Use only the transcript: if something was not said, write 'not in the call'; never guess names, amounts, dates or documents. Write amounts in Indian format (₹1,25,000), also when spoken in words ('pachaas hazaar' = ₹50,000). In these sections never copy a PAN, Aadhaar, account or card number, OTP or PIN: write [PII:PAN], [PII:AADHAAR], [PII:ACCOUNT], [PII:CARD] or [PII:OTP].

[0:00–0:25] नमस्ते, क्या मैं स्नेहा कुलकर्णी जी से बात कर रही हूँ? हाँ मैं स्नेहा बोल रही हूँ । कौन? मैं प्रिय बोल रही हूँ वरुणिका लोन पार्टनर्स से आपके पर्सनल लोन एप्लीकेशन के बारे में । ये कॉल क्वालिटी और ट्रेनिंग के लिए रिकॉर्ड हो रही है । क्या अभी दो मिन्यूट बात कर सकते हैं? हाँ, बोलिए । थैंक यू । आपकी फाइल में तीन डॉक्यूमेंट्स अभी बाकी हैं ।

[0:25–0:45] पहला जून 2026 की सैलरी स्लिप । दूसरा मार्च से मई 2026 तक का बैंक स्टेटमेंट क्योंकि लेंडर को पिछले छह महीने का स्टेटमेंट चाहिए । और तीसरा फॉर्म 16 या इतरी । अच्छा बैंक स्टेटमेंट तो मैंने जून से ऑगस्ट का दिया था । जी वो मिल गया है ।

[0:45–1:04] बस मार्च, अप्रैल और मई के 3 महीने और चाहिए । एक और बात एप्लीकेशन में आपने नेट सैलरी ₹75,000, सॉरी, ₹65,000 लिखी है लेकिन सैलरी स्लिप में नेट भी ₹18,000 है । क्या आप कन्फर्म कर सकती हैं? ₹5,000 ग्रॉस है हाथ में ₹18,000 आता है ।

[1:04–1:31] समझ गयी, मैं नोट कर लेती हूँ कि नेट सैलरी ₹18,000 है । आप ये डॉक्यूमेंट्स भेज दीजिए फिर आपका लोन पक्का अप्रूव हो जाएगा । ठीक है डॉक्यूमेंट्स कैसे भेजूँ? मैं आपको व्हाट्सएप पर एक सिक्योर अपलोड लिंक भेज रही हूँ, वो सात दिन तक वालिद रहेगा । प्लीज अपना ओ या पूरा आधार नंबर किसी को फोन पार मत बताइए । ओके कल शाम तक भेज दूँगी बहुत बढ़िया ।

[1:31–1:39] मैं कल शाम 6:00 बजे एक रिमाइंडर कॉल करुँगी । आपका दिन शुभ रहे, स्नेहा जी । थैंक यू, बाई ।

# File Check Skill

**AI reads, rules decide, you explain.** The verdict comes from a deterministic rules engine over the facts extracted from each analysed document. You only report and explain it.

## Tools

**`filecheck___list_checklists`**
Lists the loan-product checklists that the file check can apply (id, name, product, applicant type, required documents and rules).

**`filecheck___run_file_check`**
Runs the deterministic readiness check for the current project and returns `overall_verdict`, one entry per applicant (verdict, reasons, checklist, consistency, missing_items, mismatches) and lists of pending / failed / unsupported / unassigned documents.

Never pass `project_id` or `user_id`; the system injects them.

## Workflow

1. **Checklist.** If the user named a loan product or a lender / DSA brand (e.g. Varunika Loan Partners `ss_*` or Varunika Loans `ls_*` rule sets), pick its `checklist_id`. Call `filecheck___list_checklists` only when you are unsure which checklist applies AND more than one exists; if it is still ambiguous, ask with `ask_user`. Otherwise omit `checklist_id` (the default is the salaried personal loan).
2. **Run the check.** Call `filecheck___run_file_check`. Pass `applicant` (name or PAN) only when the user asks about one person.
3. **Answer** in this order:
 - `overall_verdict` and each applicant's `verdict` EXACTLY as returned: `READY` or `NOT READY`.
 - The applicant's `reasons`, verbatim.
 - A checklist table: `| Item | Status | Detail |` from `checklist` (item, status, detail).
 - A consistency table: `| Check | Status | Detail |` from `consistency` (check, status, detail).
 - Cite document names exactly as returned in `documents` / `document_name`.
 - Reasons that start with `REVIEW –` (and the `manual_review` list) are items the rules cannot verify, such as address proof, property papers or eligibility criteria. Say that a person must check them; a required REVIEW item keeps the verdict NOT READY.
4. **Never change the findings.** Do NOT change, soften, recompute, reorder or add findings, and NEVER decide READY / NOT READY yourself. If `pending_documents` is non-empty, say the verdict is provisional until those documents finish analysis. Mention `failed_documents`, `unsupported_documents` and `unassigned_documents` when present.
5. **Letters, emails, .docx or any other artifact** (e.g. a pending-documents letter): list exactly the applicant's `missing_items`, verbatim and in the same order, and list `mismatches` as items "to correct", verbatim and in the same order. Add nothing else to these lists.
6. **Search is secondary.** The search skill may be used only to quote supporting details from documents. It must never contradict the tool's verdict or findings.
7. **Errors.** If the tool returns `error` or fails, report the error to the user and do NOT guess a verdict.

# File Check Skill

**AI reads, rules decide, you explain.** The verdict comes from a deterministic rules engine over the facts extracted from each analysed document. You only report and explain it.

## Tools

**`filecheck___list_checklists`**
Lists the loan-product checklists that the file check can apply (id, name, product, applicant type, required documents and rules).

**`filecheck___run_file_check`**
Runs the deterministic readiness check for the current project and returns `overall_verdict`, one entry per applicant (verdict, reasons, checklist, consistency, missing_items, mismatches) and lists of pending / failed / unsupported / unassigned documents.

Never pass `project_id` or `user_id`; the system injects them.

## Workflow

1. **Checklist.** If the user named a loan product or a lender / DSA brand (e.g. Varunika Loan Partners `ss_*` or Varunika Loans `ls_*` rule sets), pick its `checklist_id`. Call `filecheck___list_checklists` only when you are unsure which checklist applies AND more than one exists; if it is still ambiguous, ask with `ask_user`. Otherwise omit `checklist_id` (the default is the salaried personal loan).
2. **Run the check.** Call `filecheck___run_file_check`. Pass `applicant` (name or PAN) only when the user asks about one person.
3. **Answer** in this order:
 - `overall_verdict` and each applicant's `verdict` EXACTLY as returned: `READY` or `NOT READY`.
 - The applicant's `reasons`, verbatim.
 - A checklist table: `| Item | Status | Detail |` from `checklist` (item, status, detail).
 - A consistency table: `| Check | Status | Detail |` from `consistency` (check, status, detail).
 - Cite document names exactly as returned in `documents` / `document_name`.
 - Reasons that start with `REVIEW –` (and the `manual_review` list) are items the rules cannot verify, such as address proof, property papers or eligibility criteria. Say that a person must check them; a required REVIEW item keeps the verdict NOT READY.
4. **Never change the findings.** Do NOT change, soften, recompute, reorder or add findings, and NEVER decide READY / NOT READY yourself. If `pending_documents` is non-empty, say the verdict is provisional until those documents finish analysis. Mention `failed_documents`, `unsupported_documents` and `unassigned_documents` when present.
5. **Letters, emails, .docx or any other artifact** (e.g. a pending-documents letter): list exactly the applicant's `missing_items`, verbatim and in the same order, and list `mismatches` as items "to correct", verbatim and in the same order. Add nothing else to these lists.
6. **Search is secondary.** The search skill may be used only to quote supporting details from documents. It must never contradict the tool's verdict or findings.
7. **Errors.** If the tool returns `error` or fails, report the error to the user and do NOT guess a verdict.

# Search Skill

Questions about loan-file readiness, completeness, consistency or missing documents use the **file-check** skill (`filecheck___run_file_check`) instead of search.

Do NOT mention internal search strategy or tool selection reasoning to the user. Just search and answer.

## Available Search Methods

You have these search methods. Use your judgment to pick the right combination for each query.

**`search___summarize`**
Hybrid search (vector + keyword) on uploaded documents. Returns matching content with sources.

**`WebSearch`**
Managed web search (AgentCore). Returns ranked results with source URLs, titles, and publication dates. Use only when the documents and datasets are insufficient. Always cite source URLs.

## Structured datasets (Text2SQL)

Some projects also contain **structured datasets** (spreadsheets converted to queryable tables) alongside unstructured documents. For questions needing exact numbers, aggregation, filtering, ranking, or counting ("how many", "top N", "average", "list all X where ..."), query these instead of (or in addition to) document search.

**`data___search_datasets`**
Hybrid-search the project's dataset catalog for datasets relevant to a query (returns top matches with name + description + table_name). Call this FIRST with a description of the data you need to discover which dataset(s) can answer the question. Projects may have many datasets, so search rather than list.

**`data___describe_dataset`**
Return a dataset's reference document (columns, types, enum values, query patterns, caveats) plus its `table_name`. Call this BEFORE writing SQL — it is the source of truth for column names. Columns are normalized to snake_case (e.g. `primary_type`, `sp_atk`), so no double-quoting is needed.

**`data___run_sql`**
Run a read-only DuckDB query.

- Single dataset: pass `dataset_uri`; the table is named `data` (`FROM data`).
- JOIN across datasets (e.g. multiple sheets, or two related tables): pass `dataset_uris` (a list) and reference each by its `table_name` from `describe_dataset`/`search_datasets` (e.g. `FROM t_aaa a JOIN t_bbb b ON a.code = b.code`). Include EVERY dataset your SQL touches in `dataset_uris`.

Workflow: `search_datasets` → `describe_dataset` (for each relevant dataset) → `run_sql`. Base the answer on query results and show the SQL used.

**Joining datasets**: when a question needs data combined across tables/sheets, `describe_dataset` each one to learn its columns and `table_name`, find the shared key, then issue one `run_sql` with `dataset_uris` listing all of them. Prefer a single JOIN query over stitching separate results by hand.

## Combinations

- `search___summarize` alone — quick answer from documents
- `search___summarize` with two or three differently worded queries — wider coverage
- `data___search_datasets` → `data___describe_dataset` → `data___run_sql` — exact answers from structured data
- Cross question (spans both): document search to identify the entity → `data___run_sql` with the name/keywords found → synthesize both
- Any of the above + `WebSearch` — when documents and datasets are not enough

Document/dataset search first. Web search last.

## Citations

Use inline citations naturally within the text. For document results, reference the source document and section. For web results, include the URL.

Do not fabricate information or citations that don't exist in search results.

# File Check Skill

**AI reads, rules decide, you explain.** The verdict comes from a deterministic rules engine over the facts extracted from each analysed document. You only report and explain it.

## Tools

**`filecheck___list_checklists`**
Lists the loan-product checklists that the file check can apply (id, name, product, applicant type, required documents and rules).

**`filecheck___run_file_check`**
Runs the deterministic readiness check for the current project and returns `overall_verdict`, one entry per applicant (verdict, reasons, checklist, consistency, missing_items, mismatches) and lists of pending / failed / unsupported / unassigned documents.

Never pass `project_id` or `user_id`; the system injects them.

## Workflow

1. **Checklist.** If the user named a loan product or a lender / DSA brand (e.g. Varunika Loan Partners `ss_*` or Varunika Loans `ls_*` rule sets), pick its `checklist_id`. Call `filecheck___list_checklists` only when you are unsure which checklist applies AND more than one exists; if it is still ambiguous, ask with `ask_user`. Otherwise omit `checklist_id` (the default is the salaried personal loan).
2. **Run the check.** Call `filecheck___run_file_check`. Pass `applicant` (name or PAN) only when the user asks about one person.
3. **Answer** in this order:
 - `overall_verdict` and each applicant's `verdict` EXACTLY as returned: `READY` or `NOT READY`.
 - The applicant's `reasons`, verbatim.
 - A checklist table: `| Item | Status | Detail |` from `checklist` (item, status, detail).
 - A consistency table: `| Check | Status | Detail |` from `consistency` (check, status, detail).
 - Cite document names exactly as returned in `documents` / `document_name`.
 - Reasons that start with `REVIEW –` (and the `manual_review` list) are items the rules cannot verify, such as address proof, property papers or eligibility criteria. Say that a person must check them; a required REVIEW item keeps the verdict NOT READY.
4. **Never change the findings.** Do NOT change, soften, recompute, reorder or add findings, and NEVER decide READY / NOT READY yourself. If `pending_documents` is non-empty, say the verdict is provisional until those documents finish analysis. Mention `failed_documents`, `unsupported_documents` and `unassigned_documents` when present.
5. **Letters, emails, .docx or any other artifact** (e.g. a pending-documents letter): list exactly the applicant's `missing_items`, verbatim and in the same order, and list `mismatches` as items "to correct", verbatim and in the same order. Add nothing else to these lists.
6. **Search is secondary.** The search skill may be used only to quote supporting details from documents. It must never contradict the tool's verdict or findings.
7. **Errors.** If the tool returns `error` or fails, report the error to the user and do NOT guess a verdict.

# File Check Skill

**AI reads, rules decide, you explain.** The verdict comes from a deterministic rules engine over the facts extracted from each analysed document. You only report and explain it.

## Tools

**`filecheck___list_checklists`**
Lists the loan-product checklists that the file check can apply (id, name, product, applicant type, required documents and rules).

**`filecheck___run_file_check`**
Runs the deterministic readiness check for the current project and returns `overall_verdict`, one entry per applicant (verdict, reasons, checklist, consistency, missing_items, mismatches) and lists of pending / failed / unsupported / unassigned documents.

Never pass `project_id` or `user_id`; the system injects them.

## Workflow

1. **Checklist.** If the user named a loan product or a lender / DSA brand (e.g. Varunika Loan Partners `ss_*` or Varunika Loans `ls_*` rule sets), pick its `checklist_id`. Call `filecheck___list_checklists` only when you are unsure which checklist applies AND more than one exists; if it is still ambiguous, ask with `ask_user`. Otherwise omit `checklist_id` (the default is the salaried personal loan).
2. **Run the check.** Call `filecheck___run_file_check`. Pass `applicant` (name or PAN) only when the user asks about one person.
3. **Answer** in this order:
 - `overall_verdict` and each applicant's `verdict` EXACTLY as returned: `READY` or `NOT READY`.
 - The applicant's `reasons`, verbatim.
 - A checklist table: `| Item | Status | Detail |` from `checklist` (item, status, detail).
 - A consistency table: `| Check | Status | Detail |` from `consistency` (check, status, detail).
 - Cite document names exactly as returned in `documents` / `document_name`.
 - Reasons that start with `REVIEW –` (and the `manual_review` list) are items the rules cannot verify, such as address proof, property papers or eligibility criteria. Say that a person must check them; a required REVIEW item keeps the verdict NOT READY.
4. **Never change the findings.** Do NOT change, soften, recompute, reorder or add findings, and NEVER decide READY / NOT READY yourself. If `pending_documents` is non-empty, say the verdict is provisional until those documents finish analysis. Mention `failed_documents`, `unsupported_documents` and `unassigned_documents` when present.
5. **Letters, emails, .docx or any other artifact** (e.g. a pending-documents letter): list exactly the applicant's `missing_items`, verbatim and in the same order, and list `mismatches` as items "to correct", verbatim and in the same order. Add nothing else to these lists.
6. **Search is secondary.** The search skill may be used only to quote supporting details from documents. It must never contradict the tool's verdict or findings.
7. **Errors.** If the tool returns `error` or fails, report the error to the user and do NOT guess a verdict.

---

content.text:
# Search Skill

Questions about loan-file readiness, completeness, consistency or missing documents use the **file-check** skill (`filecheck___run_file_check`) instead of search.

Do NOT mention internal search strategy or tool selection reasoning to the user. Just search and answer.

## Available Search Methods

You have these search methods. Use your judgment to pick the right combination for each query.

**`search___summarize`**
Hybrid search (vector + keyword) on uploaded documents. Returns matching content with sources.

**`WebSearch`**
Managed web search (AgentCore). Returns ranked results with source URLs, titles, and publication dates. Use only when the documents and datasets are insufficient. Always cite source URLs.

## Structured datasets (Text2SQL)

Some projects also contain **structured datasets** (spreadsheets converted to queryable tables) alongside unstructured documents. For questions needing exact numbers, aggregation, filtering, ranking, or counting ("how many", "top N", "average", "list all X where ..."), query these instead of (or in addition to) document search.

**`data___search_datasets`**
Hybrid-search the project's dataset catalog for datasets relevant to a query (returns top matches with name + description + table_name). Call this FIRST with a description of the data you need to discover which dataset(s) can answer the question. Projects may have many datasets, so search rather than list.

**`data___describe_dataset`**
Return a dataset's reference document (columns, types, enum values, query patterns, caveats) plus its `table_name`. Call this BEFORE writing SQL — it is the source of truth for column names. Columns are normalized to snake_case (e.g. `primary_type`, `sp_atk`), so no double-quoting is needed.

**`data___run_sql`**
Run a read-only DuckDB query.

- Single dataset: pass `dataset_uri`; the table is named `data` (`FROM data`).
- JOIN across datasets (e.g. multiple sheets, or two related tables): pass `dataset_uris` (a list) and reference each by its `table_name` from `describe_dataset`/`search_datasets` (e.g. `FROM t_aaa a JOIN t_bbb b ON a.code = b.code`). Include EVERY dataset your SQL touches in `dataset_uris`.

Workflow: `search_datasets` → `describe_dataset` (for each relevant dataset) → `run_sql`. Base the answer on query results and show the SQL used.

**Joining datasets**: when a question needs data combined across tables/sheets, `describe_dataset` each one to learn its columns and `table_name`, find the shared key, then issue one `run_sql` with `dataset_uris` listing all of them. Prefer a single JOIN query over stitching separate results by hand.

## Combinations

- `search___summarize` alone — quick answer from documents
- `search___summarize` with two or three differently worded queries — wider coverage
- `data___search_datasets` → `data___describe_dataset` → `data___run_sql` — exact answers from structured data
- Cross question (spans both): document search to identify the entity → `data___run_sql` with the name/keywords found → synthesize both
- Any of the above + `WebSearch` — when documents and datasets are not enough

Document/dataset search first. Web search last.

## Citations

Use inline citations naturally within the text. For document results, reference the source document and section. For web results, include the URL.

Do not fabricate information or citations that don't exist in search results.

# File Check Skill

**AI reads, rules decide, you explain.** The verdict comes from a deterministic rules engine over the facts extracted from each analysed document. You only report and explain it.

## Tools

**`filecheck___list_checklists`**
Lists the loan-product checklists that the file check can apply (id, name, product, applicant type, required documents and rules).

**`filecheck___run_file_check`**
Runs the deterministic readiness check for the current project and returns `overall_verdict`, one entry per applicant (verdict, reasons, checklist, consistency, missing_items, mismatches) and lists of pending / failed / unsupported / unassigned documents.

Never pass `project_id` or `user_id`; the system injects them.

## Workflow

1. **Checklist.** If the user named a loan product or a lender / DSA brand (e.g. Varunika Loan Partners `ss_*` or Varunika Loans `ls_*` rule sets), pick its `checklist_id`. Call `filecheck___list_checklists` only when you are unsure which checklist applies AND more than one exists; if it is still ambiguous, ask with `ask_user`. Otherwise omit `checklist_id` (the default is the salaried personal loan).
2. **Run the check.** Call `filecheck___run_file_check`. Pass `applicant` (name or PAN) only when the user asks about one person.
3. **Answer** in this order:
 - `overall_verdict` and each applicant's `verdict` EXACTLY as returned: `READY` or `NOT READY`.
 - The applicant's `reasons`, verbatim.
 - A checklist table: `| Item | Status | Detail |` from `checklist` (item, status, detail).
 - A consistency table: `| Check | Status | Detail |` from `consistency` (check, status, detail).
 - Cite document names exactly as returned in `documents` / `document_name`.
 - Reasons that start with `REVIEW –` (and the `manual_review` list) are items the rules cannot verify, such as address proof, property papers or eligibility criteria. Say that a person must check them; a required REVIEW item keeps the verdict NOT READY.
4. **Never change the findings.** Do NOT change, soften, recompute, reorder or add findings, and NEVER decide READY / NOT READY yourself. If `pending_documents` is non-empty, say the verdict is provisional until those documents finish analysis. Mention `failed_documents`, `unsupported_documents` and `unassigned_documents` when present.
5. **Letters, emails, .docx or any other artifact** (e.g. a pending-documents letter): list exactly the applicant's `missing_items`, verbatim and in the same order, and list `mismatches` as items "to correct", verbatim and in the same order. Add nothing else to these lists.
6. **Search is secondary.** The search skill may be used only to quote supporting details from documents. It must never contradict the tool's verdict or findings.
7. **Errors.** If the tool returns `error` or fails, report the error to the user and do NOT guess a verdict.

# File Check Skill

**AI reads, rules decide, you explain.** The verdict comes from a deterministic rules engine over the facts extracted from each analysed document. You only report and explain it.

## Tools

**`filecheck___list_checklists`**
Lists the loan-product checklists that the file check can apply (id, name, product, applicant type, required documents and rules).

**`filecheck___run_file_check`**
Runs the deterministic readiness check for the current project and returns `overall_verdict`, one entry per applicant (verdict, reasons, checklist, consistency, missing_items, mismatches) and lists of pending / failed / unsupported / unassigned documents.

Never pass `project_id` or `user_id`; the system injects them.

## Workflow

1. **Checklist.** If the user named a loan product or a lender / DSA brand (e.g. Varunika Loan Partners `ss_*` or Varunika Loans `ls_*` rule sets), pick its `checklist_id`. Call `filecheck___list_checklists` only when you are unsure which checklist applies AND more than one exists; if it is still ambiguous, ask with `ask_user`. Otherwise omit `checklist_id` (the default is the salaried personal loan).
2. **Run the check.** Call `filecheck___run_file_check`. Pass `applicant` (name or PAN) only when the user asks about one person.
3. **Answer** in this order:
 - `overall_verdict` and each applicant's `verdict` EXACTLY as returned: `READY` or `NOT READY`.
 - The applicant's `reasons`, verbatim.
 - A checklist table: `| Item | Status | Detail |` from `checklist` (item, status, detail).
 - A consistency table: `| Check | Status | Detail |` from `consistency` (check, status, detail).
 - Cite document names exactly as returned in `documents` / `document_name`.
 - Reasons that start with `REVIEW –` (and the `manual_review` list) are items the rules cannot verify, such as address proof, property papers or eligibility criteria. Say that a person must check them; a required REVIEW item keeps the verdict NOT READY.
4. **Never change the findings.** Do NOT change, soften, recompute, reorder or add findings, and NEVER decide READY / NOT READY yourself. If `pending_documents` is non-empty, say the verdict is provisional until those documents finish analysis. Mention `failed_documents`, `unsupported_documents` and `unassigned_documents` when present.
5. **Letters, emails, .docx or any other artifact** (e.g. a pending-documents letter): list exactly the applicant's `missing_items`, verbatim and in the same order, and list `mismatches` as items "to correct", verbatim and in the same order. Add nothing else to these lists.
6. **Search is secondary.** The search skill may be used only to quote supporting details from documents. It must never contradict the tool's verdict or findings.
7. **Errors.** If the tool returns `error` or fails, report the error to the user and do NOT guess a verdict.

The declared amount **equals the slip GROSS salary (₹65,000)**, indicating the applicant likely declared gross salary instead of net salary.

- **Net monthly income**: ₹58,000 (from salary slips, matched by bank credits)
- **Annual gross salary**: ₹7,80,000 (₹65,000 × 12, from slips)

The file check has reported these mismatches. The applicant or DSA should correct the declared net salary to ₹58,000, or provide clarification if the declared figure refers to gross salary.

- Files reach the lender incomplete and come back: READY / NOT READY file check against the lender checklist, with the missing items and months named.
- Declared salary, PAN and name are cross-checked by eye: Consistency checks with evidence; anything the rules cannot verify is marked "Needs a person".

content.text:
# File Check Skill

**AI reads, rules decide, you explain.** The verdict comes from a deterministic rules engine over the facts extracted from each analysed document. You only report and explain it.

## Tools

**`filecheck___list_checklists`**
Lists the loan-product checklists that the file check can apply (id, name, product, applicant type, required documents and rules).

**`filecheck___run_file_check`**
Runs the deterministic readiness check for the current project and returns `overall_verdict`, one entry per applicant (verdict, reasons, checklist, consistency, missing_items, mismatches) and lists of pending / failed / unsupported / unassigned documents.

Never pass `project_id` or `user_id`; the system injects them.

## Workflow

1. **Checklist.** If the user named a loan product or a lender / DSA brand (e.g. Varunika Loan Partners `ss_*` or Varunika Loans `ls_*` rule sets), pick its `checklist_id`. Call `filecheck___list_checklists` only when you are unsure which checklist applies AND more than one exists; if it is still ambiguous, ask with `ask_user`. Otherwise omit `checklist_id` (the default is the salaried personal loan).
2. **Run the check.** Call `filecheck___run_file_check`. Pass `applicant` (name or PAN) only when the user asks about one person.
3. **Answer** in this order:
 - `overall_verdict` and each applicant's `verdict` EXACTLY as returned: `READY` or `NOT READY`.
 - The applicant's `reasons`, verbatim.
 - A checklist table: `| Item | Status | Detail |` from `checklist` (item, status, detail).
 - A consistency table: `| Check | Status | Detail |` from `consistency` (check, status, detail).
 - Cite document names exactly as returned in `documents` / `document_name`.
 - Reasons that start with `REVIEW –` (and the `manual_review` list) are items the rules cannot verify, such as address proof, property papers or eligibility criteria. Say that a person must check them; a required REVIEW item keeps the verdict NOT READY.
4. **Never change the findings.** Do NOT change, soften, recompute, reorder or add findings, and NEVER decide READY / NOT READY yourself. If `pending_documents` is non-empty, say the verdict is provisional until those documents finish analysis. Mention `failed_documents`, `unsupported_documents` and `unassigned_documents` when present.
5. **Letters, emails, .docx or any other artifact** (e.g. a pending-documents letter): list exactly the applicant's `missing_items`, verbatim and in the same order, and list `mismatches` as items "to correct", verbatim and in the same order. Add nothing else to these lists.
6. **Search is secondary.** The search skill may be used only to quote supporting details from documents. It must never contradict the tool's verdict or findings.
7. **Errors.** If the tool returns `error` or fails, report the error to the user and do NOT guess a verdict.

---

content.text:
# File Check Skill

**AI reads, rules decide, you explain.** The verdict comes from a deterministic rules engine over the facts extracted from each analysed document. You only report and explain it.

## Tools

**`filecheck___list_checklists`**
Lists the loan-product checklists that the file check can apply (id, name, product, applicant type, required documents and rules).

**`filecheck___run_file_check`**
Runs the deterministic readiness check for the current project and returns `overall_verdict`, one entry per applicant (verdict, reasons, checklist, consistency, missing_items, mismatches) and lists of pending / failed / unsupported / unassigned documents.

Never pass `project_id` or `user_id`; the system injects them.

## Workflow

1. **Checklist.** If the user named a loan product or a lender / DSA brand (e.g. Varunika Loan Partners `ss_*` or Varunika Loans `ls_*` rule sets), pick its `checklist_id`. Call `filecheck___list_checklists` only when you are unsure which checklist applies AND more than one exists; if it is still ambiguous, ask with `ask_user`. Otherwise omit `checklist_id` (the default is the salaried personal loan).
2. **Run the check.** Call `filecheck___run_file_check`. Pass `applicant` (name or PAN) only when the user asks about one person.
3. **Answer** in this order:
 - `overall_verdict` and each applicant's `verdict` EXACTLY as returned: `READY` or `NOT READY`.
 - The applicant's `reasons`, verbatim.
 - A checklist table: `| Item | Status | Detail |` from `checklist` (item, status, detail).
 - A consistency table: `| Check | Status | Detail |` from `consistency` (check, status, detail).
 - Cite document names exactly as returned in `documents` / `document_name`.
 - Reasons that start with `REVIEW –` (and the `manual_review` list) are items the rules cannot verify, such as address proof, property papers or eligibility criteria. Say that a person must check them; a required REVIEW item keeps the verdict NOT READY.
4. **Never change the findings.** Do NOT change, soften, recompute, reorder or add findings, and NEVER decide READY / NOT READY yourself. If `pending_documents` is non-empty, say the verdict is provisional until those documents finish analysis. Mention `failed_documents`, `unsupported_documents` and `unassigned_documents` when present.
5. **Letters, emails, .docx or any other artifact** (e.g. a pending-documents letter): list exactly the applicant's `missing_items`, verbatim and in the same order, and list `mismatches` as items "to correct", verbatim and in the same order. Add nothing else to these lists.
6. **Search is secondary.** The search skill may be used only to quote supporting details from documents. It must never contradict the tool's verdict or findings.
7. **Errors.** If the tool returns `error` or fails, report the error to the user and do NOT guess a verdict.

I've analyzed the call transcript and found a **critical compliance issue**. Here are the **3 coaching tips** for the telecaller:

---

## Call QA Review Summary

**Recording:** `document_id:bc08a9de-500f-4984-a956-87269f3adf95` | **Caller type:** human | **Languages:** Hindi + English
**Rubric:** 0.1-draft (synthetic data)

---

### 🚨 HARD FAIL DETECTED

**H1 – Promise of approval**

> Evidence: *"फिर आपका लोन पक्का अप्रूव हो जाएगा" / "Then your loan will definitely be approved."*

This is a **hard fail** under the QA rubric. The caller promised approval, which misleads the customer and violates compliance standards.

**Score: 0 | Sent to Team Leader review**

---

## 3 Coaching Tips for Priya

### 1. Never Promise Approval — Use Conditional Language

**Issue:** Said "loan pukka approve ho jayega" (loan will definitely be approved).

**Tip:** Always use conditional, lender-neutral language that sets accurate expectations.

✅ **Better phrasing (Hindi):**
> "जब डॉक्यूमेंट्स मिल जाएँगे, फाइल लेंडर के पास चली जाएगी। फिर लेंडर अपनी प्रोसेस के हिसाब से डिसीज़न देगा।"
> *(When documents are received, the file will go to the lender. Then the lender will decide based on their process.)*

---

### 2. Clarify the Salary Discrepancy More Thoroughly

**Issue:** The salary gap (₹65,000 declared vs ₹18,000 on slip) is massive and could indicate either a typo on the application or that the loan amount will be much smaller than the customer expects.

**Tip:** When a discrepancy is this large:
- Ask the customer if the ₹65,000 was possibly a typo
- Explain gently how net salary affects eligible loan amount
- Avoid raising false expectations about the final outcome

✅ **Better approach:**
> "मैडम, ₹65,000 और ₹18,000 में बहुत फ़र्क है। क्या ये टाइपिंग मिस्टेक थी आपकी एप्लीकेशन में? जो नेट सैलरी लेंडर देखता है, उसी हिसाब से लोन अमाउंट तय होता है।"

---

### 3. Keep Security Warnings Consistent — Don't Mix Messages

**Good:** The caller correctly warned the customer NOT to share OTP or Aadhaar number over the phone — this is excellent.

**Tip:** Reinforce this by setting clear expectations about what the company will NEVER ask:
- "We will never ask for your OTP, PIN, or full Aadhaar on a call"
- "If anyone asks, hang up and call our official number"

This builds trust and protects both the customer and the company.

---

**Summary:** The call had strong elements (clear identity, proper recording disclosure, permission asked, pending documents communicated, next step agreed). But the **promise of approval is a hard fail** that nullifies everything else. Focus coaching on compliance: no guarantees, no promises — only "lender will decide based on their policy."
